samples.summary: Scope: a deployment-wide policy flip (auth webhook enforce-by-default) plus a new backend service-token identity ride in a UI-parity issue
samples.evidence: The originating work is issue #1044 (`docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md`: N1–N8 = mount `NotesToolbar` on `SharedNotesLayout`, mobile demotion, share-token uploader, session-local prefs, divider hit area, doc corrections; "Out of scope" names only sheets/board toolbars). The diff additionally (a) inverts `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` so an unset variable now DENIES (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`), (b) adds a whole new backend identity (`yorkie-service` token, `decideService`, per-side `SOURCE_JWT_SECRET`/`TARGET_JWT_SECRET` in the ops scripts), (c) read-gates `AttachDocument`, (d) suppresses presence/seed/backfill/recalc writes across sheets, slides, board, docs and pdf, (e) changes the public-template gate's contract, and (f) fixes unrelated jsdom timer teardown in `packages/docs/test/view/*`. The lessons file explains the chain (review rounds), and each piece is documented — but the consequence is that an existing self-hosted deployment which registered the webhook methods and left the variable unset silently moves from allow-all to deny on upgrade, a change no part of #1044 asked for and one an operator would look for in its own PR. Flagging the coupling, not the individual changes.

samples.summary: Top-level design docs still state shadow mode is the default, now false repo-wide
samples.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` makes enforcement the default, and `yorkie-auth-webhook.md`, the backend README and self-hosting.md were updated — but the canonical share-link doc was not: `docs/design/sharing.md:208-219` ("This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode") and :231-235 ("with the flag at its default the client-side checks are what stands there"). Same stale premise in `docs/design/template-gallery.md:668` ("with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only *shadows*"), `docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:300`, and the index entry `docs/design/README.md:155` ("shadow→enforce rollout"). Per CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline the reasoning belongs folded into the canonical subsystem docs, and sharing.md is exactly the doc a reader consults to learn whether a viewer link is write-capable.

samples.summary: New comments added by this same change assert the old shadow-by-default posture they invert
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:447` (added here) reasons "since the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", and `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:64` (added here) says "the webhook allows everything until a deployment both registers its methods and sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`" — both contradicted by `isYorkieAuthEnforced` in the same diff and by the notes design doc's own "What that wrapper is not" correction. The pre-existing sibling `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42` carries the same now-false claim ("ships in shadow mode by default … with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary") and was left untouched, so the two read-only wrappers now document opposite deployment defaults.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` re-implements `readOnlyDocStore` rather than sharing the proxy machinery, and the two already diverge
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts` (185 lines) and `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` (170 lines) are the same construct: readers allowlist, per-member memoization, `batch(fn)` passthrough, non-configurable-own-property carve-out, and identical `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` traps. Only the interface-specific bits differ (`HISTORY_METHODS`, the `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` idempotency WeakSet — both present only in the notes copy). The generic part could live once (`@wafflebase/core` ships `/geometry`, `/url`, `/image` subpaths as precedent) parameterized by a readers set; `shared-core-extraction.md:84` defers the *store abstraction*, not a generic guard helper. Cost is confined to the codebase, but it is security-sensitive trap logic that must now be fixed in two places — the divergence has already started.

samples.summary: Three different read-only mechanisms chosen in one change; the sheets one is the denylist shape this PR's own rationale argues against
samples.evidence: Within this diff notes/docs close the boundary with an allowlist Proxy whose stated point is that "a member added tomorrow is not here, so it is neutered by default" (`packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts` header), slides gates by an `options.readOnly` early return, while `YorkieStore` takes a `readOnly` boolean and adds a hand-written guard per known write path (constructor presence seed, `updateSelection`, `ensureAxisOrder`, `assertWritable` on the five comment mutators). The sheets store keeps ~40 other `doc.update()` mutators unguarded, so the next one added is a viewer-reachable write by omission — the exact failure the same PR calls out as "a list nobody remembers to extend fails open". It also mixes failure modes (throw for comments, silent no-op for presence) against the doctrine written in the read-only wrappers ("a called mutator is a silent no-op … read-only is a state the UI is expected to be usable in"). No behavioral defect today; an approach-consistency/layering mismatch.
searchedFor: packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts (ReadOnlyStore — query-result store, not a wrapper)

samples.summary: One env var, three readings — and the seed script hand-inlines instead of calling the shared helper
samples.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` reads "anything but literal `false` enforces"; `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` demands the literal `'true'`; and `register-templates.ts:157` re-implements the second inline as `config.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') !== 'true'` with a comment pointing at the helper it does not call. The divergence is argued for in the doc comments, but the net effect is that a stock enforcing deployment (variable unset) is refused by the public template tier, and a third copy of the predicate can now drift from `template-review.ts`. Calling `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` from the seed script would keep one reading per question.

samples.summary: The cross-cutting "a read-only mount may not reach doc.update()" rule is recorded only for notes and slides; pdf/sheets/docs/board docs still describe the removed writes
samples.evidence: The rule is written down in `docs/tasks/.../lessons.md` and applied in code to pdf (`activePage`, `initialRoot`), sheets (presence seed, `updateSelection`, `ensureAxisOrder`, comment mutators, cross-sheet recalc), docs (`YorkieDocStore(doc, readOnly)`) and board (selection presence), but the design docs updated are only `notes/notes.md`, `slides/slides-mobile.md` and `yorkie-auth-webhook.md`. `docs/design/pdf.md:282` still says "The viewer writes `activePage` (throttled) on scroll" and :449 pins a smoke test on a peer's `activePage` presence appearing; `docs/design/sheets/axis-id-selection.md:170-188` still documents `updateSelection`/`ensureAxisOrder` as unconditional store contracts; `docs/design/sharing.md`'s read-only-viewer section (and `docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md`, which has no read-only mention at all) does not record that a viewer now publishes no caret/selection/page presence. Behavior matches the change, but the canonical subsystem docs no longer describe it, and this is a rule future features must honor.
searchedFor: read docs/design/notes/notes.md and slides-mobile.md diff hunks

finding.summary: Scope: a deployment-wide policy flip (auth webhook enforce-by-default) plus a new backend service-token identity ride in a UI-parity issue
finding.evidence: The originating work is issue #1044 (`docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md`: N1–N8 = mount `NotesToolbar` on `SharedNotesLayout`, mobile demotion, share-token uploader, session-local prefs, divider hit area, doc corrections; "Out of scope" names only sheets/board toolbars). The diff additionally (a) inverts `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` so an unset variable now DENIES (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`), (b) adds a whole new backend identity (`yorkie-service` token, `decideService`, per-side `SOURCE_JWT_SECRET`/`TARGET_JWT_SECRET` in the ops scripts), (c) read-gates `AttachDocument`, (d) suppresses presence/seed/backfill/recalc writes across sheets, slides, board, docs and pdf, (e) changes the public-template gate's contract, and (f) fixes unrelated jsdom timer teardown in `packages/docs/test/view/*`. The lessons file explains the chain (review rounds), and each piece is documented — but the consequence is that an existing self-hosted deployment which registered the webhook methods and left the variable unset silently moves from allow-all to deny on upgrade, a change no part of #1044 asked for and one an operator would look for in its own PR. Flagging the coupling, not the individual changes.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31` makes unset mean ENFORCE (`raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'`), which is an inversion of the contract the webhook originally shipped with — `docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260712-yorkie-auth-webhook-todo.md:26` records "shadow mode: YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE (default false)". The new backend identity is real (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts`; `yorkie-auth.controller.ts:242,284` `decideService`; per-side `SOURCE_JWT_SECRET`/`TARGET_JWT_SECRET` at `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:42,258,262`), and attach is read-gated (`yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108,331-334`). The originating issue is UI-only: `docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md:12-38` is N1–N8 toolbar/mobile/uploader/prefs/divider work and its Out-of-scope section (55-58) names only sheets/board toolbars. That this branch — not some earlier one — carries the policy flip is narrated in its own lessons file (`docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:99-107,122-150,152-178`) and corroborated by the sibling correctness review of the same diff (`.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:3`). No guard makes it unreachable: the flip is the runtime default for any deployment that registered the webhook methods. The only mitigation I found is documentation (`packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185,584-605`, `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:24-32,121-140`), which records the new posture rather than negating it, and satisfies the doc-discipline half of the lens without answering the scope claim. Scope creep is explicitly in this lens's lane; whether the operator-facing deployment posture change makes it major or merely PR-hygiene minor is a judgement I cannot settle against the repo, so the finding stands.
